title: Encrypted group create response omits master_salt
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

GroupsCollectionResource._create (137-143) generates master_salt (8 bytes) and stores it on the record, but the 2.01 Created body only returns id, mcast, key_id, and master_secret.

RFC 9203 / spec 18.8.2 join_key response includes both master_secret and master_salt because both are required to derive the OSCORE Group context. The creator is an owner/member at create time and is not given the salt unless they later POST join_key to themselves.

spec 18.8.2 creation example omits salt in the prose, but the implementation already generates salt; leaving it out of the only creator-facing response makes encrypted groups unusable without a second round trip.
acceptance_criteria: Encrypted POST /groups 2.01 body includes master_salt (8 bytes) alongside master_secret and key_id, still only on the creation (and authorized join_key) path.
